label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 9
knowledgePattern: Require both quadratic branches of a modulus inequality to stay positive
solution:
For any real A,B, |A|<B is equivalent to both A<B and −A<B. Applying this gives two quadratics that must be positive for every real x:

x2+(k−3)x+5−k>0 and x2+(k+1)x+5+k>0.

Their leading coefficients are positive, so each needs a strictly negative discriminant. The discriminants simplify to (k−1)2−12 and (k−1)2−20.

Both are negative exactly when (k−1)2<12, giving 1−23<k<1+23. Equality is excluded because one quadratic would touch zero. Answer A.

hints.title: Replace the modulus by two comparisons
hints.body: An expression exceeds an absolute value exactly when it exceeds each of the two signed versions inside that absolute value.
hints.recap: An absolute-value bound has two sides that must both be respected.
hints.pitfall: The two inequalities must hold together, not as alternatives.
hints.pause: Write the two polynomial inequalities with all terms on one side.

recall.reminder: An absolute-value bound has two sides that must both be respected.

hints.title: Make each quadratic positive everywhere
hints.body: For each resulting quadratic, use its leading coefficient and discriminant to impose strict positivity for all real inputs.
hints.recap: An upward quadratic is strictly positive everywhere when its discriminant is negative.
hints.pitfall: Strictly below excludes a touching point.
hints.pause: Simplify both parameter conditions, intersect them and check equality boundaries.
